sources.title: ImportArchive — Toyota (USA) model paint-colour charts, transcribed from factory brochures; 175 model/generation pages crawled
PaintRef.com — Auto/Truck/Fleet paint cross-reference database, Toyota make (9,880 colour chips over 50 pages, plus per-model-year listings 1998-2027)
AutomotiveTouchup — Toyota code/description tables; the '<year>/all-models' page was read for every model year 1998-2026
Custom Paints Inc (usa.specialistpaints.com) — Toyota touch-up paint catalogue, product titles carry 'Name - Paint code XXX'
Toyota USA Newsroom — 2025 Camry press release; official exterior colour names (no codes published)
Toyota USA Newsroom — 2026 RAV4 press release; official exterior colour names (no codes published)

caveat: On-screen colour is approximate and for identification only. It is not a paint reference — order paint by the code.
method: Toyota exterior paint codes were assembled by crawling four independent code-to-name sources (two enthusiast databases, two touch-up-paint retailers) and keeping a code only where two or more of them agree on the colour, allowing for wording variants of the same colour and rejecting any code where the sources name different colours. Names follow the US brochure form published by ImportArchive plus its finish tag, finish is taken from that tag (mica counts as metallic) or inferred from the name where no source states one, and approxHex is ImportArchive's own chart swatch — a stylised approximation of a metallic or pearl paint, never a colorimetric value.
approxHexOmitted: An entry ships without approxHex whenever no source gives a defensible value for it, and the component draws no swatch without one — 346 of the 701 exterior entries. Ten of those were dropped deliberately after the crawl: a chart render that flattened a metallic or pearl paint to pure #000000 or #ffffff is the chart's shorthand, not the paint (Black Sand Pearl is not pure black), so a pure value is kept only on a solid finish, where it is defensible.
interior: There is no interior-trim table in this asset, and the component draws no interior swatch. No corroborated public interior trim-code list exists: the manufacturer publishes none, and the retailer and enthusiast sources that carry exterior codes carry no interior codes at all. A half-guessed trim table would put an invented name beside a real trim code, which is the one thing the unknown-code rule forbids. The interior cell stays code + the name the distributor's own catalogue resolved.
accuracy: approxHex is an approximation of paint under unknown light and is never a colorimetric value. It comes from a brochure-derived chart swatch, drawn to be legible in a list: reds are systematically over-saturated, greys, silvers, whites and blues read true. A code is one name here although a manufacturer reuses codes across decades, which is why a name the host's own backend resolved always wins over this one. Coverage is US-market biased, so a deployment whose vehicles are built for another market will see more codes go unresolved — which renders as the code alone, the correct answer for a code the catalogue does not know.
